title: The metadata table reads version 1 while the file name reads v2
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
section: Metadata table, rows Document and Version
description: The metadata table of the source reads Version 1 and Date 28 October 2026, while the file name reads v2. The next version cannot carry both readings as its own version, and the family rule takes the file name.
evidence: Metadata table: Version 1, Date 28 October 2026; file name Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
proposed: Take the file name as the family version, so this version is 3, and keep the source reading in a Source version row of the metadata table and in the change log.

title: The decision log archive rule keeps a copy in the data lake
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
section: 1. Retention schedule, proposed, row Decision log
description: The source states that the decision log is copied to the data lake. Architecture v5 removes the data lake and removes the Power BI feed, and the decision log becomes a local record plus a central ledger in rwb-decision.
evidence: Source row: Decision log, DP12, Archive: Copy kept in the data lake. Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 37 and plan DP-17: no data lake; ADR-018 and ADR-022.
proposed: Keep the 10-year period and replace the archive rule with the central decision ledger of rwb_decision, the local decision record and the rwb.decision-record.v1 topic.

title: Scores (DP11) have no owning schema and no table
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
description: The source gives Scores (DP11) a 2-year period and a delete action but names no store. No table in the Physical Schema v6 carries DP11 and no service schema is named for it; the only read is the ACE view v_ace_score through the ACE view contract.
evidence: Physical Schema v6: no table with data product DP11; Logical Data Model v8 LOV-DATA-PRODUCT DP11 Scores and route economics and DF-ACE-270 to DF-ACE-279 v_ace_score; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 for the P1 ACE view contract.
proposed: Name the record against the read that supplies it, v_ace_score through rwb-source-data, keep the 2-year delete period, and let the ACE owner apply it.

title: No retention period for tables that carry no data-product row
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
section: 1. Retention schedule, proposed, and 1.1 Retention by schema
description: The source schedule is per data product and document type (DL26). The target also has tables with no data-product row: the loads and operations tables of rwb_source_data and rwb_integration, the reporting tables of rwb_reporting and the agent tables of rwb_agent. No period is given for them anywhere in the run sources.
evidence: Logical Data Model v8 subject areas OPS, RPT and AGT carry no DP code on interface_config, job_catalog, outbound_item, reconciliation_result, data_product_load, measure_definition, measure_snapshot, measure_publish, agent_policy, agent_prompt, agent_run, agent_evaluation and agent_sample; DL26 asks for a value per data product and document type.
proposed: State the placeholder in the three schema rows that hold only such tables and leave the period to the bank retention schedule when Compliance issues it under DL26.

title: A legal hold on a party or a document has no field in the target
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
description: The source allows a hold on a case, a party or a document. The target gives only recovery_case.legal_hold and status_before_hold in rwb_case; no table for a party or a document has a hold flag, and no operation places such a hold.
evidence: Physical Schema v6: recovery_case.legal_hold and recovery_case.status_before_hold; document and party_ext have no hold column; Ownership Map v1: only POST /cases/{caseId}/legal-hold is a hold operation.
owner_role: Legal counsel with P3 rwb-case and P5 rwb-document
proposed: Record the hold on the case and have the P5 retention job exclude every document of a held case, as the P5 acceptance criteria already assume.

title: No operation or event lets the retention job act on another service's schema
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
description: The source has one monthly job that lists, reviews, approves and destroys records. Retention is owned by P5 rwb-document, but the rows sit in 19 schemas and no service may write another service's tables. Neither the API Specification nor the Event and Messaging Design has an expiry or destroy operation or event.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 ruling: retention is P5 rwb-document; plan DP-01 and ADR-014: one schema per service, no cross-schema reads or writes; API Specification v4 and Event and Messaging Design v4: no retention or expiry path.
proposed: Let the owner of each schema act on its own rows, and let the P5 decision reach it over that service's REST contract, one hop with a 2 s timeout, until an expiry event is added to the catalog.

title: The access-log period refers to a bank standard that is not in the run sources
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
section: 1. Retention schedule, proposed, row Access log
description: The access log row gives the period as per the bank security standard and names no store. The target gives rwb-access the access log and serves GET /admin/access-log, but no access-log table is in the Physical Schema v6 and the standard itself is not in the run documents.
evidence: Source row: Access log, data product None, Per the bank security standard, Archive. Ownership Map v1: GET /admin/access-log is x_module P4. Physical Schema v6: no access log table.
proposed: Keep the period and the archive rule as written, name rwb-access as the owner, and leave the store and the standard to the security design and the bank retention schedule.

title: The retention class LAKE_COPY has no target without the data lake
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
section: 1. Retention schedule, proposed, row Decision log, and 3. How destruction happens
description: retention_rule.record_class carries LAKE_COPY for the decision log lake copy. With the data lake removed the class describes no record, while the decision log stays excluded from the monthly job by the table_name rule.
evidence: Physical Schema v6 comment on retention_rule.record_class: Retention class from LOV-RETENTION, or LAKE_COPY for the decision log lake copy; comment on retention_rule.table_name: never decision_log_entry; Architecture v5 slide 37 and plan DP-17.
proposed: Retire the LAKE_COPY class with the lake and keep the exclusion of decision_log_entry and the JOB-14 hash-chain check.

title: No source maps a data product to a service schema
source: 10 Policy, controls and compliance/Recovery Workbench Records Retention and Archiving v2.docx
description: The schedule is per data product, and the target is per schema. The Ownership Map gives a table and an endpoint owner, but no source gives the mapping from DP01 to DP14 to the 19 schemas.
evidence: Ownership Map v1 Tables and Endpoints sheets: table and path owners only; Logical Data Model v8 LOV-DATA-PRODUCT: product codes only; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41: service scope in words.
proposed: Read the mapping from the owner of the tables that carry each data product, and name a record against every schema that holds part of it.
